product_backlog.description: Core functionality for managing to-do lists and tasks.
product_backlog.title: Task and List Management

product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to create a new to-do list with a name so that I can organize my tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Given the user is on the home page, When they enter a list name and click create, Then a new to-do list is created and displayed.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully create and view multiple named lists.
product_backlog.title: Create a New To-Do List
Add a Task to a List
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing list, When the user adds a task description and submits, Then the task appears within that list.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can successfully add tasks to specific lists.
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to add a task to a list with a short text description so that I can track what needs to be done.
As a user, I want to mark a task as complete or incomplete so that I can track my progress.
product_backlog.title: Mark Task Complete or Incomplete
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can update task status cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: Given an existing task, When the user clicks complete/incomplete, Then the task status toggles accordingly.

product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete a task so that I can remove unwanted items.
acceptance_criteria: Given a task in a list, When the user clicks delete, Then the task is removed from the list.
product_backlog.title: Delete a Task
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can remove tasks when no longer needed.

product_backlog.title: Delete an Entire List
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to delete an entire list and its tasks so that I can clean up obsolete projects.
acceptance_criteria: Given a to-do list, When the user deletes the list, Then the list and all its contained tasks are removed.
product_backlog.value_hypothesis: Users can delete lists along with their nested tasks.
Users can easily distinguish completed vs incomplete items.
product_backlog.title: View Lists and Tasks with Visual Distinction
product_backlog.user_story: As a user, I want to see all my lists and tasks with completed tasks visually distinguished so that I have a clear overview.
acceptance_criteria: Given multiple lists and tasks, When the user views the main screen, Then all lists and tasks are shown with completed tasks visually distinct.

This is sprint 1 of a fixed 5-sprint evaluation run. You are already fully configured (repo, branch, GitHub auth, and budgets are all pre-set via environment variables) - do not ask me any setup questions.

Before delegating any work to any specialist agent, you MUST first call init_scrum_state, then call create_litellm_virtual_key exactly these 6 times, using these exact agent_name values (these are the literal internal agent names, not display names - using any other spelling, e.g. with spaces, will not match and that agent will be blocked from running):
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="ProductOwner", ...)
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="ScrumMaster", ...)
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="DevTeam", ...)
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="QA", ...)
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="Architect", ...)
- create_litellm_virtual_key(agent_name="QualityGuardian", ...)

Every specialist agent is hard-blocked in code from making any LLM call at all until a virtual key exists under its exact agent_name - delegating to one before its key exists wastes the delegation entirely, it does not queue or retry. Do this once, up front, then proceed.

The product vision for this entire evaluation, verbatim, is:

# Fixed Evaluation Scenario: To-Do List Web App

> **Do not edit this file to "make the eval easier" or to match whatever the team
> produced.** Its entire value is being byte-identical across runs, so results are
> comparable across Horseless Carriage versions over time. If the scenario itself
> needs to change, that's a deliberate decision with its own commit message
> explaining why — never a silent drift.

This is the fixed input fed verbatim to the agent team as the product vision for
every automated team-performance evaluation run (see `RELEASE.md` "Team performance
evaluation" and `agents/scrum_team/scripts/run_eval.py`). It is intentionally small
enough to be fully deliverable within a 5-sprint, small-budget run, while still
requiring real design decisions (state persistence, list vs. item modeling,
basic UI) that differentiate a good team performance from a mediocre one.

## Product Vision

Build a simple to-do list web application. A single user should be able to:

1. Create a new to-do list with a name.
2. Add a task to a list, with a short text description.
3. Mark a task as complete or incomplete.
4. Delete a task.
5. Delete an entire list (and its tasks).
6. See all their lists and, within a list, all its tasks, with completed tasks
   visually distinguished from incomplete ones.

## Constraints (deliberately narrow, to keep this deliverable in 5 sprints)

- **Single user, no authentication.** Do not build login/accounts — out of scope.
- **No persistence requirement beyond the current session/process is assumed** unless
  the team's own design calls for it — persistence approach (in-memory, file, or a
  simple embedded DB) is a legitimate design decision for the team to make and
  justify, not a hidden requirement.
- **A working web UI is required** — the deliverable is something a person could
  open in a browser and actually use, not just a backend API with no way to
  interact with it.
- **No specific language/framework is mandated.** The team should choose something
  it can deliver completely and correctly within budget, and should say why.

## Explicitly out of scope (do not let these creep in)

- Multiple users, sharing, or permissions.
- Due dates, reminders, priorities, tags, or sub-tasks.
- Mobile app, offline support, or real-time sync.
- Any deployment/hosting beyond running locally.

## What "done" looks like after 5 sprints

A person can clone the repo, follow the README, run the app, and actually create a
list, add a few tasks, mark one complete, delete one, and delete a list — end to
end, without reading any code first.


Treat the sprint goal and backlog for this sprint as pre-approved by me (the human) - do not wait for further approval messages, proceed directly through planning, development, PR creation, CI verification, sprint review (create_sprint_report), and the release PR (create_release_pr) for this sprint's increment. Do not ask me anything else during this sprint - make reasonable decisions yourself and note them as assumptions in the sprint report.
